23394.boardCall: Odds ratio 1.2 with 95% CI 0.64-2.23 -> not statistically significant because CI includes 1.0.
23394.hinge: A confidence interval for an odds ratio that spans 1.0 indicates that the association is not statistically significant.

A.tempting: excluding zero indicates statistical significance in differences

B.clue: Relying on point estimate without variance
B.fit: Not here: point estimate alone cannot establish significance without confidence interval analysis
B.tempting: odds ratio of 1.2 suggests increased risk

C.clue: Asserting case-control studies cannot assess association
C.fit: Not here: case-control studies properly estimate odds ratios as a measure of association
C.tempting: case-control studies cannot directly calculate relative risk

D.clue: Accurate identification of nonsignificant confidence interval
D.fit: Here: 95% CI 0.64-2.23 spans 1.0, failing to achieve statistical significance

algorithm.title: Interpreting odds ratios and confidence intervals

nodes.text: Calculate odds ratio (OR) in case-control study: ratio of odds of exposure in cases vs controls
Evaluate 95% confidence interval relative to the null value of 1.0
**Confidence interval includes 1.0 (0.64-2.23):** result is not statistically significant (p >= 0.05)
**Confidence interval excludes 1.0 entirely:** statistically significant association
Do not claim significant association based solely on a point estimate exceeding 1.0
Assess potential confounding, recall bias, and selection bias inherent in case-control designs

nodes.text: Atypical subtrochanteric fractures are a medication adverse effect of long-term alendronate due to suppressed bone remodeling.
Stop alendronate, protect weight bearing, and obtain bilateral femur radiographs.
**Persistent focal thigh pain despite negative radiographs:** obtain MRI for an incomplete stress fracture.
**Complete fracture:** arrange operative fixation, usually with an intramedullary nail.
**Painful incomplete fracture with a visible fracture line:** consider prophylactic intramedullary fixation.
**High fragility-fracture risk after stopping alendronate:** consider teriparatide with a bone specialist.

**BPP score <= 4 or oligohydramnios:** proceed to urgent delivery

Hysteroscopy with adhesiolysis: restore uterine cavity patency if Asherman confirmed

23541.hinge: On a box plot, the median represents the 50th percentile and the upper hinge represents the 75th percentile.

algorithm.title: Box plot distribution and quartile interpretation

nodes.text: Analyze box plot components: minimum, Q1 (25th percentile), median (50th), Q3 (75th), maximum
Locate pathologic cutoff line relative to the box plot anatomy
**Cutoff falls between median (Q2) and Q3:** 50% to 75% of values lie below cutoff
**Cutoff falls below Q1:** fewer than 25% of values lie below cutoff
Recognize that the interquartile range (IQR = Q3 - Q1) contains the middle 50% of observations
Evaluate asymmetry in box hinges or whiskers to assess skewness in data distribution

23542.hinge: One-way ANOVA compares the means of a continuous dependent variable across three or more independent categorical groups.
23542.trap: Comparing group means tempts two-sample t-test, but multiple group comparisons require ANOVA to prevent type I error inflation.

A.clue: Compares continuous means across >= 3 groups
A.fit: Here: continuous insulin sensitivity compared across 3 groups (PIs, naive, controls)

B.clue: Nonparametric test evaluating categorical independence
B.fit: Not here: dependent variable (insulin sensitivity) is continuous, not categorical counts
B.tempting: evaluating proportions across multiple groups

C.clue: Bivariate linear association test between continuous variables
C.fit: Not here: independent variable is categorical (3 treatment groups), not continuous
C.tempting: assessing linear association between two variables

D.clue: Parametric test comparing continuous means between 2 groups
D.fit: Not here: restricted to 2 groups; using t-test across 3 groups inflates alpha error
D.tempting: standard test comparing continuous group means

E.clue: Parametric test comparing proportions between 2 groups
E.fit: Not here: applies to dichotomous categorical outcomes, not continuous measurements
E.tempting: testing proportions across study samples

algorithm.title: Selecting statistical tests for group comparisons

nodes.text: Identify independent variable (categorical: 3 treatment groups) and dependent variable (continuous: insulin sensitivity)
Determine number of independent groups being compared
**Continuous outcome across >= 3 groups:** select one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA)
**Continuous outcome between exactly 2 groups:** select two-sample independent t-test
**Categorical outcome across groups:** select chi-square test of independence
Perform post-hoc pairwise testing (Tukey HSD) if ANOVA reveals overall statistical significance

23603.boardCall: Vaccine RR 0.25 -> relative risk reduction is 75% in vaccinated infants.
23603.hinge: Relative risk reduction (RRR) equals 1 minus the relative risk; an RR of 0.25 yields a 75% risk reduction.

A.tempting: miscalculating cross-product ratios

B.tempting: confusing risk ratio with odds calculation

C.fit: Not here: 25% is the relative risk (RR = 0.25), not the risk reduction
C.tempting: interpreting relative risk of 0.25 as 25% reduction

E.tempting: observational studies lack experimental randomization

algorithm.title: Cohort study risk ratios and relative risk reduction

nodes.text: Calculate incidence in vaccinated cohort: 10 cases / 200 vaccinated infants = 0.05 (5%)
Calculate incidence in unvaccinated cohort: 40 cases / 200 unvaccinated infants = 0.20 (20%)
Calculate relative risk (RR): incidence in exposed / incidence in unexposed (0.05 / 0.20 = 0.25)
**Relative risk reduction (RRR):** calculated as 1 - RR (1 - 0.25 = 0.75 or 75% risk reduction)
**Absolute risk reduction (ARR):** calculated as unexposed minus exposed incidence (0.20 - 0.05 = 0.15 or 15%)
Calculate number needed to vaccinate (NNV): reciprocal of ARR (1 / 0.15 = 6.7, rounds to 7)

algorithm.title: Cognitive bias and diagnostic error in endometriosis

nodes.text: Chronic pelvic pain + cyclic bowel symptoms (dyschezia, diarrhea): avoid premature closure
Recognize anchoring bias: attributing severe pelvic symptoms solely to irritable bowel syndrome
Perform comprehensive pelvic examination + transvaginal ultrasound
**Endometrioma or deep infiltrating nodules visualized:** initiate targeted hormonal or surgical care
**Ultrasound negative but high suspicion:** diagnostic laparoscopy for definitive tissue diagnosis
Implement diagnostic time-outs and re-evaluate when symptoms fail conservative management

nodes.text: Subacute tender cervical lymphadenopathy after cat exposure suggests Bartonella henselae infection.
Give oral azithromycin to hasten nodal shrinkage.
**Fluctuant painful node:** perform needle aspiration.
**Visual symptoms with optic disc edema or macular star:** involve ophthalmology and consider doxycycline plus rifampin.
**Atypical, prolonged, or disseminated presentation:** pursue Bartonella serology or tissue PCR as part of targeted evaluation.

nodes.text: A water-bottle cardiac silhouette after tuberculosis suggests a large pericardial effusion.

Send sampled pericardial fluid for mycobacterial culture and adenosine deaminase.
Start rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for tuberculous pericarditis.
**HIV-negative with a large inflammatory effusion or early constriction:** consider adjunctive prednisolone.

nodes.text: Posterior uveitis + recent rash or oral mucous patches → suspect ocular syphilis
RPR/VDRL + treponemal immunoassay
**Serology positive + cranial nerve or other neurologic findings:** LP with CSF-VDRL
**Serology positive, isolated ocular findings:** treat without required LP
IV aqueous crystalline penicillin G for 10–14 days
**Penicillin allergy:** desensitization, then IV penicillin
**Anterior uveitis + inflammatory back pain:** HLA-B27 spondyloarthritis instead
Test HIV and other STIs

19126.boardCall: Term infant + cyanosis refractory to 100% O2 + clear lungs -> cyanotic congenital heart defect -> echocardiogram.
19126.hinge: Persistent cyanosis and low PaO2 despite 100% supplemental oxygen indicates a cyanotic congenital heart defect.
19126.trap: Severe cyanosis tempts immediate intubation or sepsis antibiotics, but normal work of breathing requires echocardiography first.

A.clue: Infectious workup and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics
A.fit: Not here: afebrile, refractory cyanosis without respiratory distress points to CCHD
A.tempting: cyanosis in early newborn period

B.clue: Transthoracic ultrasound of cardiac structure and function
B.fit: Here: term neonate, refractory hypoxemia PaO2 43 mm Hg on 100% oxygen

C.clue: Endotracheal tube placement and mechanical ventilation
C.fit: Not here: lungs clear, no retractions, failed hyperoxia test indicates shunt
C.tempting: low oxygen saturation of 75% in newborn

D.clue: Spectrophotometric assessment of oxidized hemoglobin
D.fit: Not here: severe cyanotic shunt, right-to-left cardiac defect is vastly more common

E.clue: Intravenous volume expansion for hypovolemic shock
E.fit: Not here: full peripheral pulses, well perfused extremities, normotensive
E.tempting: newborn with cyanosis and low venous saturation

nodes.text: Cyanotic term newborn: administer 100% oxygen and perform hyperoxia test
**PaO2 > 150 mm Hg:** pulmonary parenchymal etiology (TTN, RDS, aspiration)
**PaO2 < 100 mm Hg despite 100% O2:** cyanotic congenital heart defect (CCHD)
Perform emergent transthoracic echocardiogram to identify cardiac anatomy
Initiate IV prostaglandin E1 (alprostadil) infusion to maintain ductal patency
**Ductal-dependent lesion on echo:** urgent pediatric cardiology and surgical consultation

triggers.text: cyanosis is noted over the lips, trunk, and extremities
There are no retractions, grunting, or stridor.
Breath sounds are normal.
receiving 100% oxygen shows: pH 7.32 PaCO2 38 mm Hg PaO2 43 mm Hg

19404.hinge: Compression of the lower trunk (C8-T1) at the thoracic outlet produces medial hand dysesthesias with arm elevation.
19404.trap: Fifth digit numbness tempts ulnar nerve compression at the wrist, but reproduction with arm elevation confirms thoracic outlet syndrome.

A.tempting: upper extremity numbness in active adult

nodes.text: C8–T1 lower-trunk compression at the thoracic outlet produces medial hand paresthesias with arm elevation.
Examine strength, sensation, and pulses. Obtain radiographs for a cervical rib.
Begin posture and shoulder-girdle physical therapy for neurogenic symptoms.
**Unilateral arm swelling or cyanosis:** obtain urgent duplex for subclavian venous thrombosis.
**Cool hand or digital ischemia:** obtain urgent vascular assessment for arterial compression or embolization.
**Progressive weakness or muscle wasting despite physical therapy:** refer for decompression evaluation.

19419.boardCall: Continuous infraclavicular murmur + bounding pulses -> patent ductus arteriosus -> LV volume overload.
19419.hinge: A large patent ductus arteriosus produces left-to-right shunting, causing left ventricular volume overload with preserved contractility.
19419.trap: Tachypnea and an S3 gallop can tempt contractile dysfunction, but PDA produces hyperdynamic high-output failure.

A.clue: Left ventricular outflow obstruction with myocardial failure
A.fit: Not here: bounding peripheral pulses, continuous murmur, not diminished pulses
A.tempting: infant heart failure with tachypnea and poor feeding

B.clue: Severe afterload elevation with compensated ejection fraction
B.fit: Not here: normal blood pressure 86/40, no pulse delay or systolic ejection murmur
B.tempting: infant with signs of left heart stress

nodes.text: Left-to-right shunting through PDA causes left ventricular volume overload with preserved contractility
Identify exam features: continuous machinery murmur + bounding pulses + wide pulse pressure
Perform echocardiogram: confirm PDA diameter, shunt direction, and left atrial/LV enlargement
Initiate medical management: furosemide for volume overload
**Preterm infant with significant shunt:** trial cyclooxygenase inhibitor (indomethacin or ibuprofen)
**Term infant or failed medical therapy:** transcatheter device closure or surgical ligation

19434.boardCall: Early personality change + social disinhibition + new compulsions -> behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.
19434.hinge: Severe social disinhibition and novel compulsive behaviors in a 65-year-old identify frontotemporal dementia.
19434.trap: Neglecting bills and chores tempts Alzheimer dementia, but striking disinhibition and rituals distinguish FTD.

A.clue: Early prominent episodic short-term memory impairment
A.fit: Not here: prominent behavioral disinhibition and hyperorality overshadow mild memory complaints
A.tempting: difficulty remembering how to perform routine household chores

B.clue: Focal frontal and temporal neurodegeneration causing behavioral changes
B.fit: Here: social disinhibition, hugging strangers, new smoking, compulsive TV rituals

C.clue: Late-onset psychosis with persecutory delusions and hallucinations
C.fit: Not here: loss of executive function and disinhibition without hallucinations
C.tempting: sudden religious preoccupation and inappropriate behavior

D.clue: Treponemal central nervous system infection with tabes dorsalis
D.fit: Not here: progressive frontotemporal atrophy pattern without focal neurological signs
D.tempting: bizarre disinhibited behaviors and personality change

E.clue: Stepwise cognitive decline following cerebrovascular infarctions
E.fit: Not here: insidious behavioral decline without focal focal neurologic deficits
E.tempting: older patient with executive dysfunction and chore difficulty

nodes.text: Early social disinhibition and new compulsive behaviors suggest behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia.
Obtain brain MRI for frontal or anterior temporal atrophy and evaluate for reversible contributors.
**MRI nondiagnostic despite a convincing behavioral syndrome:** consider specialist FDG-PET for frontotemporal hypometabolism.
**Disinhibition or compulsions disrupt care despite environmental changes:** consider sertraline.
Provide caregiver education and structured routines. Avoid donepezil for frontotemporal dementia.

recently started smoking and has tried to kiss and hug strangers
offered to have sex with younger men whom she does not know well

19506.boardCall: Asymptomatic uncontrolled hypertension despite two-drug regimen -> medication nonadherence.
19506.hinge: Medication nonadherence is the most common reason for persistent hypertension in asymptomatic patients.
19506.trap: Persistently high blood pressure tempts secondary renal causes, but nonadherence is far more common.

A.clue: Medial arterial calcification causing pseudohypertension
A.fit: Not here: age 45, no end-stage renal disease or diabetes
A.tempting: resistant systolic blood pressure elevation

B.clue: Suboptimal initial antihypertensive drug selection
B.fit: Not here: lisinopril plus amlodipine is a first-line synergistic combination
B.tempting: blood pressure unchanged after 3 months of therapy

C.clue: Patient failure to take prescribed pharmacological therapy
C.fit: Here: asymptomatic patient, blood pressure 158/95 on two drugs, normal exam

D.clue: Myocardial remodeling from longstanding afterload stress
D.fit: Not here: ventricular hypertrophy is a target organ consequence, not cause

E.clue: Intrinsic nephropathy causing volume expansion and hypertension
E.fit: Not here: unremarkable physical exam, nonadherence is vastly more prevalent
E.tempting: refractory blood pressure elevation requiring dual therapy

nodes.text: Nonadherence with therapy: most common cause of persistently elevated blood pressure
Explore adherence nonjudgmentally: ask about pill routines, side effects, and cost
**Regimen complexity barrier:** simplify regimen to single combination pill + pillbox reminders
Confirm true hypertension: obtain 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
**Adherence confirmed on 3 drugs including diuretic:** screen for secondary hypertension
Start lifestyle interventions: DASH diet + sodium restriction + exercise

triggers.text: patient feels well and is currently asymptomatic
blood pressure of 160/96 mm Hg
combination of lisinopril and amlodipine was prescribed
Today, his blood pressure is 158/95 mm Hg.

19728.hinge: Synpharyngitic hematuria with RBC casts and normal serum complement indicates IgA nephropathy.
19728.trap: Postinfectious glomerulonephritis produces low complement 1-3 weeks after infection, whereas IgA has normal complement.

A.clue: Nephrotic-range proteinuria with pyuria
A.fit: Not here: glomerular nephritic pattern with RBC casts, not leukocyte casts
A.tempting: urinary abnormalities after acetaminophen use

B.clue: Severe acute tubular necrosis sediment
B.fit: Not here: normal kidney perfusion, recurrent glomerular hematuria after URI
B.tempting: dark urine following febrile illness

C.clue: Glomerular inflammation with normal serum complement
C.fit: Here: dark urine days after URI, prior hematuria episode, hypertension

D.clue: Hypocomplementemic poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
D.fit: Not here: IgA nephropathy has normal complement; PSGN occurs 1-3 weeks later
D.tempting: hematuria and hypertension following upper respiratory infection

E.clue: Ischemic tubular necrosis with normal complement
E.fit: Not here: RBC casts present, dark urine is glomerular hematuria
E.tempting: dark urine mistaken for tubular cast formation

F.fit: Not here: no dysuria or fever, normal complement in IgA nephropathy
F.tempting: abnormal urine in young female patient

algorithm.title: Post-URI hematuria: IgA nephropathy vs PSGN

nodes.text: Gross hematuria following upper respiratory tract infection: check complement and urinalysis
**IgA nephropathy (synpharyngitic, within 5 days):** normal C3/C4 + RBC casts
**PSGN (poststreptococcal, 1-3 weeks later):** low C3 + elevated ASO/anti-DNase B
Monitor blood pressure + calculate spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio
Initiate ACE inhibitor or ARB for persistent proteinuria > 0.5-1 g/day
**Rapidly rising creatinine:** renal biopsy to assess crescentic glomerulonephritis

19995.hinge: Twelve months without conception despite regular ovulatory cycles and normal semen analysis warrants further evaluation; AMH assesses ovarian reserve.
19995.trap: Regular menstrual cycles can tempt invasive laparoscopy, but noninvasive ovarian reserve testing must come first.

A.clue: Serum marker reflecting total functional ovarian reserve
A.fit: Here: 12 months infertility, normal semen analysis, regular 26-day cycles

B.clue: Autoimmune thrombophilia serologic panel
B.fit: Not here: nulligravid patient with primary infertility, no miscarriages
B.tempting: autoimmune workup in patient with celiac disease

C.fit: Not here: invasive surgical procedure; noninvasive hormonal testing precedes laparoscopy
C.tempting: moderate cramping with menses suggesting endometriosis

D.clue: Chromosomal analysis for aneuploidy or translocations
D.fit: Not here: normal pubertal development, regular menses, no recurrent miscarriages

E.tempting: young age of 31 with regular menstrual periods

nodes.text: After 12 months without conception at age 31, assess both partners; regular cycles usually indicate ovulation.
Measure antimüllerian hormone to assess ovarian reserve and expected stimulation response.
With normal semen and regular cycles, obtain hysterosalpingography to assess tubal patency.
**Bilateral tubal occlusion:** refer for in vitro fertilization evaluation.
**Anovulation due to PCOS with patent tubes:** induce ovulation with letrozole.
**Ovulation, semen, and tubal evaluation normal:** consider ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination.

20017.boardCall: Tube-fed patient + fever + concentrated urine + hypernatremia -> inadequate free water replacement.
20017.hinge: Hypotonic fluid loss from fever in an obtunded patient on fixed tube feeds produces hypernatremia from free water deficit.
20017.trap: Hyperconcentrated urine osmolality might tempt diabetes insipidus, but urine osm 1100 proves intact ADH response.

A.clue: Adrenal cortical insufficiency causing salt wasting
A.fit: Not here: causes hyponatremia and hyperkalemia, not hypernatremia
A.tempting: hypotension and altered mental status

B.clue: Defective renal collecting duct aquaporin water channels
B.fit: Not here: urine osmolality is 1,100 mOsm/kg, proving intact concentrating ability
B.tempting: elevated serum sodium with altered sensorium

C.clue: Unreplaced insensible hypotonic fluid losses from fever
C.fit: Here: fever 39.1 C, diaphoresis, fixed enteral feeds, sodium 152 mEq/L

D.clue: Hyperglycemia-driven solute diuresis in proximal tubules
D.fit: Not here: glucose 184 mg/dL is below renal threshold for osmotic diuresis
D.tempting: history of type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypernatremia

nodes.text: Obtunded patient on fixed tube feeds with fever: free water losses not replaced
Urine osmolality > 800 mOsm/kg: intact renal concentration
**Polyuria with urine osmolality < 300 mOsm/kg:** diabetes insipidus; desmopressin challenge
**Recent hypertonic saline or bicarbonate:** sodium overload; D5W + loop diuretic
Free water deficit = TBW × (Na/140 − 1)
Enteral free water flushes or IV D5W
**Hypotension:** isotonic saline first
Lower sodium ≤ 10–12 mEq/L per 24 hours

A.clue: Positional nystagmus testing for canalithiasis
A.fit: Not here: no vertigo or nystagmus, acute peripheral facial nerve palsy
A.tempting: acute neurologic presentation with abnormal sensation

B.fit: Here: left facial melting, inability to sip from straw, intact sensation

algorithm.title: Bell palsy evaluation and corneal protection

nodes.text: Acute unilateral upper and lower facial weakness (forehead involved): diagnose Bell palsy
Perform eyelid closure evaluation: assess for lagophthalmos and Bell phenomenon
**Incomplete eye closure:** prescribe daytime artificial tears + nighttime lubricating ointment + eye tape
Prescribe oral corticosteroid therapy (prednisone for 10 days) within 72 hours of onset
**Severe facial paralysis (House-Brackmann IV-VI):** add oral valacyclovir
Re-evaluate within 2-4 weeks to monitor motor recovery and corneal integrity

20179.hinge: Paroxetine's short half-life triggers antidepressant discontinuation syndrome when irregular shift work causes missed doses.
20179.trap: Shift-work insomnia tempts melatonin, but acute anxiety, dizziness, and muscle aches indicate antidepressant discontinuation.

A.fit: Not here: misses underlying medication discontinuation syndrome from skipped paroxetine
A.tempting: frequently alternating between day and night shifts

B.fit: Not here: somatic symptoms stem from missed medication, not primarily workplace fatigue
B.tempting: patient feels stressed by job as security guard

C.clue: Minimizing symptoms with watchful waiting
C.fit: Not here: acute discontinuation symptoms will persist or worsen without adherence

D.clue: Attributing somatic symptoms to hyperthyroidism
D.fit: Not here: normal physical exam, paroxetine timing explains abrupt symptoms

nodes.text: On short-acting paroxetine: abrupt anxiety, headache, restlessness, aches
Ask nonjudgmentally about schedule disruption and missed doses
**Recent missed doses:** restart paroxetine; symptoms resolve within 24 hours
**Patient wants to stop:** slow taper over weeks to months
**Recurrent missed doses from shift work:** switch to fluoxetine (long half-life)
Adherence aids: phone alarms, pillbox

20214.hinge: Collaborative dietary counseling that identifies lower-calorie substitutions within cultural staples optimizes diabetes management.
20214.trap: Offering generic handouts or prescribing a Mediterranean diet ignores the patient's native culinary staples and reduces adherence.

A.fit: Not here: ignores patient's Costa Rican culinary traditions and reduces adherence
A.tempting: Mediterranean diet is widely proven beneficial for diabetes

B.clue: Collaborative calorie reduction preserving cultural food staples
B.fit: Here: Costa Rican immigrant, prepares meals at home, rising A1c and weight

C.clue: Distributing standardized Spanish educational brochures
C.fit: Not here: software engineer speaks English, generic brochures fail to engage
C.tempting: providing translated materials for Hispanic immigrant

D.fit: Not here: small office snack contributes minimally compared to daily home staples
D.tempting: patient eats midday snack from office break room

algorithm.title: Culturally sensitive dietary counseling for diabetes

nodes.text: Ask about usual meals, preparation methods, budget, and the patient's dietary goals.
Discuss lower-calorie alternatives for the patient's customary staple foods.
Agree on feasible portions or cooking changes that preserve preferred dishes.
**Food cost or access limits choices:** identify affordable substitutions and connect the patient with nutrition support.
**A1c remains above the individualized goal:** review adherence and reassess medication options alongside nutrition counseling.

prepares her own breakfast and dinner at home most days

20234.hinge: A DNR order specifically directs withholding cardiopulmonary resuscitation at the time of cardiac arrest.
20234.trap: A DNR order does not preclude active management of acute medical illness prior to cardiac arrest.

A.clue: Partial resuscitation with mechanical support exclusion
A.fit: Not here: standard DNR withholds all cardiopulmonary resuscitation interventions
A.tempting: distinguishing chest compressions from mechanical ventilation

B.clue: Total prohibition of endotracheal intubation for any indication
B.fit: Not here: intubation for non-arrest reversible respiratory failure may be permitted unless DNI specified
B.tempting: assuming DNR always forbids intubation before arrest

C.clue: Allowing invasive ventilation during cardiac arrest
C.fit: Not here: DNR precludes intubation during cardiac arrest resuscitation attempts
C.tempting: providing airway support without chest compressions

D.clue: Complete cessation of resuscitation efforts upon cardiac arrest
D.fit: Here: DNR order on file, clarifies natural death at cardiac arrest

E.clue: Withholding all life-prolonging treatments prior to arrest
E.fit: Not here: DNR does not withhold antibiotics, diuresis, or inpatient medical therapy
E.tempting: confusing DNR with comfort measures only

algorithm.title: Code status determination and DNR interpretation

Define DNR order scope: applies exclusively to the event of cardiac or respiratory arrest

algorithm.title: Obstructive sleep apnea in Down syndrome

nodes.text: Adult Down syndrome with new daytime somnolence, irritability, or cognitive skill decline
Recognize high anatomical risk: midface hypoplasia, macroglossia, and pharyngeal hypotonia
Obtain overnight polysomnography to diagnose obstructive sleep apnea
**OSA confirmed (AHI >= 5):** initiate continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy
**CPAP intolerance:** evaluate for dental appliances, tonsillectomy, or hypoglossal nerve stimulation
Reassess behavioral and cognitive functioning after restoring sleep architecture

nodes.text: Fever, cytopenias, and adrenal enlargement during anti-TNF therapy in an endemic area suggest disseminated histoplasmosis.
Obtain urine and serum Histoplasma antigen and fungal blood cultures.

**Disseminated disease without organ failure or systemic toxicity:** consider itraconazole with specialist input.
**Shock or suspected adrenal crisis:** give IV hydrocortisone and isotonic fluid promptly.
Hold anti-TNF treatment during active infection and monitor response with serial antigen testing.

23346.boardCall: Blood splash onto intact skin from untreated HIV patient -> wash with soap and water, no PEP needed.
23346.hinge: HIV exposure to intact skin carries no risk of transmission; thorough washing with soap and water is sufficient without PEP.
23346.trap: Untreated HIV with high viral load tempts postexposure prophylaxis, but intact unbroken skin provides an impermeable barrier.

A.clue: Immediate washing with soap and water
A.fit: Here: splash of HIV blood onto intact neck and arm, skin cleaned, no PEP

B.clue: Source immune cell staging to determine transmission risk
B.fit: Not here: CD4 count does not guide PEP decision; exposure is non-transmissible
B.tempting: quantifying patient immunodeficiency

C.clue: Source quantitative viremia measurement
C.fit: Not here: intact skin carries zero transmission risk regardless of viral load
C.tempting: checking viral load in patient off antiretroviral therapy

D.clue: Baseline recipient testing with contingent prophylaxis
D.fit: Not here: baseline test only detects preexisting infection, but no exposure occurred

E.clue: Immediate three-drug antiretroviral postexposure regimen
E.fit: Not here: intact skin exposure does not transmit HIV; PEP exposes to unnecessary toxicity
E.tempting: patient has untreated HIV with high transmission risk

nodes.text: Wash occupational blood from skin with soap and water; irrigate exposed mucosa.
**Blood contacted intact skin only:** reassure; no additional testing or HIV PEP is needed.
**Percutaneous, mucosal, or nonintact skin exposure to potentially infectious blood:** evaluate promptly and start HIV PEP if warranted.
**Source tests HIV negative without concern for acute infection:** discontinue HIV PEP.
For significant exposures, assess hepatitis B immunity and arrange hepatitis C follow-up based on source testing.

triggers.text: chronic HIV infection that has been treated with antiretroviral medications
splashes the patient's blood and contaminated irrigation solution on her exposed neck and upper arm
The exposed skin is intact, and all visible blood is cleaned with soap and water.
protective equipment for the face and eyes

23380.boardCall: Rh-negative mother + spontaneous abortion -> administer anti-D immune globulin.
23380.hinge: An unsensitized Rh-negative patient with pregnancy loss at 13 weeks by dates should receive anti-D immune globulin.
23380.trap: Heavy vaginal bleeding and passage of tissue tempt suction curettage, but hemodynamic stability and closed cervix prioritize Rh prophylaxis.

A.clue: Passive antibody prophylaxis against fetal RhD antigen
A.fit: Here: spontaneous abortion, vaginal bleeding, maternal blood type O Rh-negative

B.clue: Parenteral broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage
B.fit: Not here: afebrile 37.3 C, no foul-smelling discharge or uterine fundal purulence
B.tempting: fever and abdominal cramping with abortion

C.clue: Minimally invasive diagnostic pelvic visualization
C.fit: Not here: intrauterine tissue passed, ultrasound shows intrauterine endometrium
C.tempting: adnexal cyst with free fluid in cul-de-sac

D.clue: Prostaglandin E1 analogue with progesterone antagonist
D.fit: Not here: patient has completed or nearly completed spontaneous abortion
D.tempting: medical management of early pregnancy loss

E.clue: Endometrial evacuation via negative pressure cannula
E.fit: Not here: hemodynamically stable, closed cervical os, minimal active bleeding
E.tempting: passage of blood clots and tissue with cramping

algorithm.title: Early pregnancy loss and Rh alloimmunization prevention

nodes.text: Evaluate pregnancy loss with ultrasound, hemodynamic assessment, blood type, and antibody screen.
**Unsensitized Rh-negative patient with pregnancy loss at 13 weeks by dates:** give anti-D immune globulin.
**Loss before 12 weeks:** routine Rh testing and anti-D may be forgone after individualized discussion.
**Retained tissue without hemorrhage or infection:** offer expectant management, misoprostol, or uterine aspiration.
**Hemorrhagic instability or suspected septic abortion:** resuscitate and arrange urgent uterine evacuation.
**Suspected infection:** give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics promptly.
Offer bereavement support and follow-up.

triggers.text: intense lower abdominal cramps along with vaginal bleeding
noticed some tan-colored tissue intermixed with large blood clots
cervix is closed, and the uterus is 6-week-sized
maternal blood type is O, Rh negative

abdominal-wall-disorders.name: Abdominal wall disorders
abdominal-wall-disorders.scope: Rectus sheath hematoma, Fothergill sign, epigastric hernia, umbilical hernia, incisional hernia, diastasis recti
abdominal-wall-disorders.core: A focal abdominal-wall mass or pain persisting with muscle contraction suggests a wall lesion rather than visceral disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Anticoagulation, severe cough, pregnancy, trauma → rectus bleeding
Prior laparotomy, obesity, wound infection → incisional defect; increased intra-abdominal pressure promotes hernias

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Fothergill sign**: palpable rectus mass remains fixed during contraction, does not cross midline
Carnett sign: tenderness unchanged/increased with tensing supports abdominal-wall pain
★ Irreducibility with pain, vomiting, skin discoloration → incarceration/strangulation
Diastasis: broad midline ridge with head raising; intact fascia, no incarceration

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Epigastric vessel or muscle injury → blood confined within rectus sheath
Fascial defect permits fat/bowel protrusion; linea alba stretching separates rectus muscles in diastasis

rows.label: Dx
items: Standing examination with Valsalva; assess reducibility, obstruction and peritoneal signs
★ Suspected hematoma → **CBC, coagulation studies, CT**; contrast identifies active extravasation
Ultrasound for uncertain superficial hernia; CT for complex postoperative anatomy or bowel compromise

rows.label: Tx
items: Stable hematoma → analgesia, observation, hold/reverse anticoagulation when bleeding warrants
★ Hemodynamic instability → resuscitation/transfusion; persistent arterial bleeding → **embolization**
Strangulated or obstructed hernia → urgent operation; avoid forceful reduction
Symptomatic adult hernia → elective repair; diastasis → reassurance, core rehabilitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Hematoma → anemia, hemorrhagic shock; operative exploration can disrupt tamponade
Hernia → bowel ischemia/perforation; repair → infection or recurrence

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight management, smoking cessation, constipation/cough control; careful anticoagulant monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Appendicitis: visceral/peritoneal findings, pain often decreases with tensing
Intra-abdominal tumor: mass becomes less palpable with abdominal contraction

abdominal-wall-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

acetaminophen-toxicity.name: Acetaminophen toxicity
acetaminophen-toxicity.scope: Rumack-Matthew nomogram, 4-hour post-ingestion level, toxic metabolite NAPQI, N-acetylcysteine indications and timing, acute liver failure
acetaminophen-toxicity.core: Potentially toxic acetaminophen ingestion can be asymptomatic initially; time-specific concentration and hepatic injury determine immediate N-acetylcysteine treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intentional overdose, repeated excessive dosing, unrecognized combination cold/pain products
Malnutrition and chronic heavy alcohol use increase vulnerability, especially with repeated supratherapeutic use
Extended-release products and opioid/anticholinergic co-ingestion may delay absorption

rows.label: Clues
items: First day: nausea/vomiting or no symptoms; next 1–3 days: RUQ pain, rising AST/ALT
★ **Coagulopathy, hypoglycemia, encephalopathy**, acidosis → severe hepatic failure
Early normal transaminases and clinical improvement do not establish safety

rows.label: Pathophys
items: CYP metabolism produces NAPQI; glutathione depletion → centrilobular hepatocyte necrosis
N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and benefits established liver failure beyond toxin clearance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Known acute ingestion → **acetaminophen concentration at ≥4 hours**; earlier result cannot risk-stratify
★ Plot **Rumack–Matthew nomogram**, 4–24 h; treatment line starts 150 µg/mL at 4 h
Unknown timing/repeated supratherapeutic use → no nomogram; obtain concentration, AST/ALT, INR, glucose, creatinine
Delayed absorption and initial detectable subthreshold level → repeat concentration after 4–6 h
Assess co-ingestions/pregnancy; intentional ingestion → psychiatric safety evaluation after stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ At/above treatment line → **N-acetylcysteine**, ideally within 8 h; benefit persists when delayed
Likely substantial ingestion and result delayed beyond 8 h → start antidote while awaiting testing
Unknown time: >10 µg/mL or liver injury; repeated excess: ≥20 µg/mL or abnormal aminotransferases → treat
Recent acute overdose, protected airway → activated charcoal, usually within 4 h; toxicology consultation
Continue antidote until clearance and hepatic/coagulation recovery criteria met; acute liver failure → transplant center

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant hepatic failure, AKI, cerebral edema, hypoglycemia, death
IV antidote → non-IgE-mediated infusion reaction; pause/treat reaction, then resume when needed

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Count acetaminophen across all products**, avoid duplicate dosing, secure storage
Assess suicide risk and arrange mental-health care after deliberate ingestion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic hepatitis: preceding profound hypotension
Viral hepatitis: exposure/serology without toxic ingestion pattern

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

acute-rhinosinusitis.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
acute-rhinosinusitis.scope: Common cold, viral rhinosinusitis, acute bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria, symptomatic therapy, antibiotic stewardship
acute-rhinosinusitis.core: Acute nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and facial pressure usually reflect a self-limited viral infection; duration and course identify likely bacterial disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Respiratory exposure, daycare contacts, impaired drainage from allergic inflammation
Immunocompromise, recent antibiotics, or hospitalization increases resistant-organism risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough, reduced smell, maxillary tenderness; colored mucus alone does not establish bacterial infection
★ Orbital swelling, painful eye movement, reduced vision, severe headache → **complicated infection**
Well febrile child, URI symptoms, clear lungs, good perfusion: soft flow murmur innocent, not VSD

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral mucosal edema blocks sinus drainage; secondary infection commonly pneumococcus, H influenzae, or Moraxella

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; uncomplicated illness needs neither sinus radiographs nor CT
Persistent, severe, or biphasic course identifies bacterial cases; fever alone is insufficient
Suspected orbital/intracranial extension → contrast CT; MRI for intracranial definition
Refractory or unusual infection → ENT evaluation; routine nasal swab cultures unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Viral illness → **saline irrigation, acetaminophen/NSAID**, oral pseudoephedrine (not young children); no antibiotics
Intranasal fluticasone for associated allergic inflammation; topical oxymetazoline at most 3 days
★ Uncomplicated bacterial illness + reliable follow-up → **watchful waiting** or antibiotics
Antibiotic choice: amoxicillin-clavulanate, usually 5–7 days in adults; penicillin allergy → doxycycline
Complication → admission, IV ampicillin-sulbactam, urgent ENT/ophthalmology; avoid empiric azithromycin because resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Orbital cellulitis or abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis, meningitis, intracranial abscess
Unnecessary antibiotics → diarrhea, C difficile, resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, smoking avoidance, control allergic rhinitis
Sterile/distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, watery discharge without fever
Migraine: episodic disabling headache, photophobia, nausea
Dental infection: focal tooth pain, unilateral maxillary symptoms

table.title: Bacterial patterns
rows: Initial improvement → new fever or worsening symptoms

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.name: Adolescent confidentiality and care
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.scope: Confidentiality principles, exceptions to parental notification, parental requests for drug testing, encouraging family involvement
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.core: Provide adolescents private, developmentally appropriate care; explain confidentiality and its safety limits before sensitive questions.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality supports honest disclosure; consent authority and parental access vary by jurisdiction
Assent: involve the adolescent even when guardian permission remains necessary
Contraception: minors generally consent confidentially; no parental notice or pelvic exam required

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview alone** for sexual health, substance use, mood, violence, and safety
★ Explain permitted confidential services; protect portals, billing, and result notifications
Encourage trusted-adult involvement; never require disclosure for legally confidential services

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Parental request for **drug testing** → discuss concern, interview teen; avoid covert testing
Do not promise absolute secrecy or automatically send sensitive findings to parents
Do not breach for experimental substance use without impairment → counsel, schedule **follow-up visit**

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Imminent danger, suspected **abuse/neglect/exploitation** → protective disclosure and reporting
Emergency treatment when delay risks serious harm; involve guardians when feasible
Emancipated minors generally self-consent; pregnancy alone does not universally confer emancipation

rows.label: Traps
items: Minor consent varies: STI, contraception, pregnancy, mental health, substance; **elective surgery** → parents
Mandatory reporting thresholds for consensual sexual activity depend on ages and local law
Disclose minimum necessary information; explain safety-driven disclosure to adolescent whenever feasible

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; jurisdiction-specific consent/reporting law must be verified locally.

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

advance-directives-and-surrogates.name: Advance directives and surrogate decisions
advance-directives-and-surrogates.scope: Living will, DNR/DNI orders, health care proxy, substituted judgment, best interests, advance care planning
advance-directives-and-surrogates.core: Follow the capable patient's current wishes; when capacity is absent, use valid directives and authorized surrogate judgment.

rows.label: Principle
items: Autonomy persists after incapacity through documented preferences and legally authorized decision-makers
Substituted judgment: patient's known values; best interests: benefits/burdens when preferences unknown

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Confirm capacity, directive validity, clinical applicability, and designated **health care proxy**
★ Apply the patient's instructions over conflicting surrogate preferences
Discuss goals, code status, surrogate early; terminal sole caregiver → plan **child guardianship**

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ **DNR limits CPR**; do not automatically withhold antibiotics, analgesia, nutrition, or other treatment
Dementia diagnosis, mild test errors, or disagreement ≠ incapacity; capacity is decision-specific
★ **Surrogate cannot compel contraindicated treatment** → withhold it; ethics consult unnecessary

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Capable patient may revise prior instructions; current informed choices control
No directive/proxy → adult next of kin; none eligible (minor relative) → **court guardian**
Clear directive/reported wishes/proxy–team agreement → no consult; unresolved conflict → ethics, court

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **DNI and DNR differ**; clarify acceptable ventilation and perioperative plans
Proxy needs no terminal illness; dementia tube-feeding request → review lack of benefit, harms
Surrogate conveys patient's known wishes, not own beliefs; missing paperwork doesn't block them

table.title: Documents and authority
rows: Durable health care power of attorney
Current medical order limiting specified intervention
Portable treatment orders for serious illness

advance-directives-and-surrogates.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics framework; document validity and surrogate hierarchy depend on jurisdiction.

alopecia.name: Alopecia
alopecia.scope: Alopecia areata (smooth patches, exclamation mark hairs, intralesional triamcinolone), androgenetic alopecia (minoxidil, finasteride), telogen effluvium, trichotillomania, tinea capitis
alopecia.core: Hair loss with intact follicular openings suggests nonscarring alopecia. Inspect distribution, hair shafts, and scalp before choosing therapy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Areata: autoimmune predisposition, especially thyroid disease. Androgenetic: family history
Telogen effluvium: fever, surgery, childbirth, or rapid weight loss **2–3 months** earlier
Tinea capitis: school-age child, affected contacts, shared combs

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Areata: **exclamation mark hairs** taper toward scalp. Nail pitting
Androgenetic in women: widened central part with preserved frontal hairline
Tinea: posterior cervical nodes or boggy inflammatory **kerion**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Areata: T-cell attack on anagen follicles. Androgenetic: DHT-driven follicular miniaturization
Telogen effluvium: synchronized shift into resting phase

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected tinea → **KOH microscopy** and fungal culture of plucked hairs or scalp scale
Telogen effluvium: diffusely positive hair-pull test. Unexplained shedding → CBC, ferritin, TSH

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pediatric areata → **topical clobetasol**. Severe adult areata → dermatology for baricitinib
★ Androgenetic in men → consider **oral finasteride**. Avoid finasteride in pregnancy
★ Kerion → start antifungal while culture pending. Topical monotherapy inadequate for scalp infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Kerion may leave permanent scarring. Areata may progress to total scalp or body hair loss

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tinea transmission: avoid sharing headwear and brushes. Adjunct selenium sulfide shampoo reduces shedding of spores

rows.label: Mimics
items: Traction alopecia: marginal loss along tight hairstyles, preserved fringe hairs
Discoid lupus: scarred, dyspigmented plaques with follicular plugging
Secondary syphilis: moth-eaten patches with generalized rash or adenopathy

table.title: Nonscarring patterns and initial therapy
rows: Men: bitemporal recession and vertex thinning
Irregular patches, broken hairs of varying lengths

alopecia.evidence: Checked AAD hair loss guidance, FDA baricitinib label, CDC tinea treatment and habit-reversal trial, Nov 2026.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amniotic-fluid-embolism.name: Amniotic fluid embolism
amniotic-fluid-embolism.scope: Cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, acute hypoxemia, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), massive transfusion protocol, supportive critical care
amniotic-fluid-embolism.core: Abrupt hypoxemia, cardiovascular collapse, and DIC during labor or shortly after delivery suggest amniotic fluid embolism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Labor, cesarean/vaginal delivery, placental disruption; unpredictable and usually unpreventable
Reported associations: advanced maternal age, abnormal placentation, induction; associations do not establish causation

rows.label: Clues
items: Sudden dyspnea, cyanosis, agitation, seizure, profound hypotension, fetal bradycardia
★ **Bleeding from IV sites or uterine hemorrhage** with falling fibrinogen suggests consumptive coagulopathy
May present chiefly as coagulopathy; absence of the full triad early does not exclude disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal inflammatory response to amniotic components triggers pulmonary vasoconstriction and coagulation activation
Acute right ventricular failure may progress to left ventricular dysfunction and pulmonary edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis of exclusion**; no definitive blood test or imaging marker
ABG, CBC, PT/aPTT, fibrinogen, crossmatch; bedside echocardiography helps characterize shock
Fetal squamous cells in pulmonary circulation are neither necessary nor specific
Exclude hemorrhage, pulmonary thromboembolism, anaphylaxis, high neuraxial block, eclampsia without delaying resuscitation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **High-quality CPR**, left uterine displacement, oxygenation/intubation; activate obstetric/anesthesia/critical-care teams
Vasopressors/inotropes guided by echocardiography; avoid fluid overload with RV failure
★ **Massive transfusion protocol**: red cells, plasma, platelets; replace fibrinogen with cryoprecipitate/concentrate
Arrest, uterus ≥umbilicus, no ROSC → resuscitative delivery: start by 4 minutes, birth by 5
Operate at arrest location without transport delay; consider ECMO for refractory cardiopulmonary failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxic brain injury, multiorgan failure, exsanguination, maternal death; fetal hypoxic injury/death

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pulmonary embolism: thrombotic risk, RV strain; immediate profound DIC less characteristic
Anaphylaxis: trigger exposure, urticaria/bronchospasm; treat epinephrine
Hemorrhagic shock: bleeding precedes collapse, rather than unexplained respiratory failure first

amniotic-fluid-embolism.evidence: Resuscitation checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM updated AFE checklist, 2026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13565333/); clinical patterns established teaching.

ankle-and-foot-injuries.name: Ankle and foot injuries
ankle-and-foot-injuries.scope: Lateral ankle sprain, Ottawa ankle and foot rules, RICE therapy, functional rehabilitation, Achilles tendon rupture, plantar fasciitis, calcaneal apophysitis
ankle-and-foot-injuries.core: Mechanism, focal tenderness, weight-bearing ability, and tendon function distinguish ankle sprain from fracture and overuse foot disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Inversion while plantarflexed, prior sprain, poor balance → lateral ligament injury
Running/jumping, sudden training increase, tight calves, obesity; fluoroquinolones/steroids increase tendon rupture risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Lateral swelling after inversion → **anterior talofibular ligament** injury most likely
Pain above ankle with external rotation/squeeze → syndesmotic sprain; recovery slower
Focal bony pain, deformity, neurovascular changes, or inability to bear weight → fracture evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ligament overstretch → microtears or disruption; tendon degeneration predisposes rupture
Repeated loading damages soft tissue; tendon degeneration reduces tensile strength

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ankle pain + **posterior-edge/tip malleolar tenderness** → ankle radiographs
★ Midfoot pain + **navicular or fifth-metatarsal-base tenderness** → foot radiographs
Either region: inability to take four steps immediately and during evaluation also triggers corresponding radiographs
Examine skin, pulses, sensation; persistent focal pain despite normal films → reassess occult fracture

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sprain: **protection, ice, compression, elevation**, brief analgesia; early protected weight-bearing
Functional brace + range-of-motion, strength, proprioceptive rehabilitation; avoid prolonged routine immobilization
Displaced/open fracture or neurovascular compromise → urgent orthopedics; immobilize and keep non-weight-bearing

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic instability, recurrent sprains, osteochondral talar injury
Missed syndesmotic injury → prolonged disability; immobilization → stiffness, thrombosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Balance training and bracing** after prior sprain; gradual return when strength/function restored
Gradual training progression, supportive footwear, calf flexibility; avoid premature athletic return

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lisfranc injury: plantar ecchymosis, midfoot instability; weight-bearing radiographs
Septic arthritis: fever, marked passive-motion pain; aspirate joint

table.title: Heel disorders
rows: Pop, weak plantarflexion, abnormal Thompson test
First-step morning pain; medial plantar heel
Active child; posterior heel squeeze tenderness

ankle-and-foot-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic decision rules and rehabilitation principles.

anorectal-disorders.name: Anorectal disorders
anorectal-disorders.scope: Anal fissure, internal and external hemorrhoids, anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, pruritus ani, topical vasodilators, fiber, sitz baths
anorectal-disorders.core: Anal pain, bleeding, swelling, or drainage requires inspection and focused examination; pain pattern distinguishes fissure, thrombosis, and infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constipation, straining, pregnancy, prolonged sitting; Crohn disease, diabetes, immunosuppression increase infection risk
Irritant soaps, moisture, fecal seepage contribute to pruritus ani

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion, fever, spreading erythema, crepitus** → evaluate necrotizing perineal infection urgently
Posterior midline fissure common; lateral/multiple fissures suggest Crohn disease, infection, or malignancy
Internal hemorrhoids lie above dentate line; prolapse may require manual reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fissure causes internal sphincter spasm and local ischemia; hemorrhoids represent enlarged vascular cushions
Cryptoglandular infection creates abscess; persistent epithelialized tract can become a fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspection first**, gentle DRE/anoscopy when tolerable; do not force painful fissure examination
Deep pain without visible lesion → CT/MRI for occult abscess; recurrent fistula → pelvic MRI
Rectal bleeding with anemia, weight loss, bowel change, or screening indication → colon evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fiber, fluids, stool softening, **sitz baths**; fissure → topical anesthetic, nitroglycerin or diltiazem
Refractory chronic fissure → botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy after continence-risk assessment
Internal hemorrhoids persisting despite conservative measures → rubber-band ligation; advanced prolapse → surgery
★ Abscess → **incision and drainage**; antibiotics added for cellulitis, systemic illness, or immunosuppression
Fistula → colorectal surgery; painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid within 72 hours → consider excision

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess recurrence, fistula, sepsis; sphincter injury → fecal incontinence
Chronic bleeding → iron deficiency; pruritus → excoriations and secondary infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid straining and prolonged toilet sitting; gentle cleansing, dry skin, barrier ointment for seepage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anal cancer: persistent irregular ulcer/mass or large wart-like lesion, biopsy required
Proctitis: urgency, tenesmus, mucous discharge
Pinworm: nocturnal itch, especially children; tape test

table.title: Local patterns
rows: Tearing defecation pain; bright blood on paper
Recurrent purulent drainage from external opening

anorectal-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established colorectal teaching.

antepartum-fetal-surveillance.name: Antepartum fetal surveillance
antepartum-fetal-surveillance.scope: Nonstress test (reactive vs nonreactive), biophysical profile (BPP components and scoring), modified BPP, contraction stress test, umbilical artery Doppler, indications (FGR, diabetes, post-term, decreased movement)
antepartum-fetal-surveillance.core: Assess fetal well-being when stillbirth risk is elevated; abnormal screening generally needs confirmation or delivery according to gestation and severity.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ FGR, high-risk diabetes, hypertension, post-term pregnancy, decreased fetal movement

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Often around 32 weeks; earlier if severe risk and delivery would be considered
Decreased movement → prompt NST/fluid assessment; ongoing frequency based on underlying disorder

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Reactive NST ≥32 weeks: **two 15-beat accelerations lasting 15 seconds**, within 20 minutes
Before 32 weeks use 10 × 10; extend observation to 40 minutes for sleep
★ **BPP**: NST plus four ultrasound components; each 0 or 2, maximum 10

rows.label: IF positive
items: Nonreactive NST → stimulation/extended tracing, then BPP or selected contraction stress test
★ BPP ≤4 generally → delivery; 6 → repeat within 24 hours or term delivery
Low fluid requires evaluation despite score; umbilical Doppler guides FGR decisions

rows.label: Traps
items: BPP 8–10 reassuring only with normal fluid; modified BPP = NST + fluid assessment
CST: late decelerations with ≥50% contractions positive; avoid when labor contraindicated
False positives common; reassuring test does not predict acute abruption or cord accident

table.title: Ultrasound BPP: normal criteria during 30-minute observation

antepartum-fetal-surveillance.evidence: Indications checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG surveillance guidance](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2021/06/indications-for-outpatient-antenatal-fetal-surveillance); interpretation established obstetric teaching.

antidepressants.name: Antidepressants
antidepressants.scope: SSRIs, SNRIs, bupropion, mirtazapine, tricyclic antidepressants (anticholinergic toxicity, urinary retention, arrhythmia), MAO inhibitors, adverse effects (serotonin syndrome)
antidepressants.core: SSRIs usually start depression treatment; choose alternatives by accompanying symptoms, adverse effects, and overdose risk.

rows.label: Use
items: SSRIs/SNRIs: depression, anxiety; duloxetine also neuropathic pain
Bupropion: smoking cessation; mirtazapine: poor appetite with insomnia
TCAs/MAOIs: resistant depression; TCAs also neuropathic pain

rows.label: Mechanism
items: SSRIs: serotonin reuptake blockade; SNRIs/TCAs: serotonin + norepinephrine reuptake blockade
Bupropion: norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake blockade; mirtazapine: α2 antagonism
MAOIs: reduced monoamine degradation

rows.label: Adverse
items: SSRIs: GI upset, SIADH, bleeding; SNRIs: ↑BP; mirtazapine: sedation/weight gain; bupropion: activating
★ SSRI **sexual dysfunction** → **lower dose** first; other SSRIs rarely help; bupropion minimal
TCAs: constipation, urinary retention, conduction toxicity; MAOIs: orthostatic hypotension

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ Bupropion lowers seizure threshold: **seizure or eating disorders**; CYP inhibitors raise levels
TCAs: urinary retention, glaucoma, conduction disease; anticholinergic delirium in older adults
TCA therapy with QTc/QRS prolongation → **stop TCA**, no waiting for levels

rows.label: Interactions
items: MAOI + tyramine/sympathomimetics → hypertensive crisis → **phentolamine** (α-blocker)
MAOI + SSRI/tramadol → serotonin syndrome; washout generally 14 days, after fluoxetine 5 weeks
Fluoxetine/paroxetine inhibit CYP2D6 → ↑TCA levels, toxicity

rows.label: Monitor
items: Mood, suicidality early in young adults; monitor adherence and functioning
Abrupt stop → **discontinuation**: flu-like aches, headache, dizziness, electric paresthesias, nausea, tremor
Response over 4–6 weeks; taper to stop, especially paroxetine and venlafaxine

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Serotonin syndrome**: clonus, fever/agitation → stop drugs, benzodiazepines; cyproheptadine
★ TCA overdose: Na⁺-channel blockade → **wide QRS**, arrhythmia, seizures → IV sodium bicarbonate
Bipolar depression: antidepressant monotherapy may provoke mania

antidepressants.evidence: Not checked online; established pharmacology and prescribing safety.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

aortic-dissection.name: Aortic dissection
aortic-dissection.core: Sudden maximal chest or back pain with vascular or neurologic deficits suggests aortic dissection, even without widened mediastinum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long-standing hypertension → **medial degeneration** in older adults; bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation
Marfan/vascular Ehlers-Danlos, pregnancy, cocaine, aortic instrumentation or aneurysm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Abrupt severe pain**, pulse/BP asymmetry, syncope, focal neurologic deficit
New aortic regurgitation murmur; limb ischemia or abdominal pain from branch-vessel malperfusion
Hypotension suggests rupture, tamponade, severe regurgitation, or coronary involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear → blood separates medial layers, creating false lumen
Propagation compromises branch arteries or ruptures into pericardium/pleura

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable → **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis**; unstable or unable to leave resuscitation → bedside TEE
Chest radiograph may show widened mediastinum but normal film does not exclude dissection
ECG/troponin may mimic MI; high suspicion requires aortic imaging before antithrombotics
Examine bilateral arm pressures, femoral pulses, neurologic status, renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV esmolol or labetalol** + opioid analgesia; target HR 60–80 and SBP <120 if perfusion maintained
Persistent hypertension after rate control → nicardipine or nitroprusside; avoid vasodilator before beta blockade
★ **Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis** when dissection suspected
Tamponade from dissection → immediate surgical team; routine pericardiocentesis can worsen hemorrhage

rows.label: Complications
items: Aortic rupture, hemothorax, tamponade, MI, stroke, paraplegia, mesenteric/renal ischemia
Late aneurysmal dilation or recurrent dissection despite initial successful treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lifelong **BP control and surveillance CTA/MRA**; beta-blocker-based regimen
Avoid heavy isometric lifting; screen first-degree relatives for familial aortopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute coronary syndrome: pressure-like pain, no pulse deficit; coexistence possible
PE: pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, right-heart strain
Esophageal rupture: vomiting followed by pain and subcutaneous emphysema

aortic-dissection.evidence: Not checked online; established aortic emergency principles.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

atheroembolic-disease.name: Atheroembolic disease
atheroembolic-disease.scope: Cholesterol crystal embolization, vascular procedures, livedo reticularis, blue toe syndrome, acute kidney injury, eosinophilia and hypocomplementemia, supportive management
atheroembolic-disease.core: Delayed kidney injury plus livedo reticularis or painful blue toes after arterial instrumentation suggests cholesterol crystal embolization.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Extensive aortic atherosclerosis, older age, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, peripheral arterial disease
★ Recent **angiography, vascular surgery**, or aortic manipulation; occasionally spontaneous plaque disruption
