items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Antibody → **paternal antigen typing**; negative (certain paternity) → no fetal risk; else fetal typing, titers
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Sensitizing event → dose now; lasts ~12 weeks, repeat at 28; postpartum only if Rh-positive/unknown infant
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

table.title: Early and routine pregnancy calls
rows: Nausea, irregular bleeding or amenorrhea, even premenarche
Missed menses, urinary frequency, friable cervix, enlarged uterus
Brief sharp movement-triggered lower-quadrant pain, normal vitals
No added preterm, fluid, or placental risk

scabies.name: Scabies
scabies.scope: Sarcoptes scabiei infestation, pruritus worse at night, burrows in web spaces and flexures, mineral oil scraping, topical permethrin, oral ivermectin, household contact treatment
scabies.core: Contagious mite infestation causing intense nocturnal itching, especially when household members also itch; eradicate infestation and treat exposed contacts simultaneously.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged skin contact, sexual exposure, crowded households, nursing facilities
Immunosuppression, neurologic impairment, advanced age → crusted disease with enormous mite burden

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Burrows in finger webs**, flexor wrists, axillae, waist, genitalia; excoriated papules/nodules
Adults usually spare head; infants may involve scalp, face, palms and soles
Crusted form: widespread hyperkeratotic plaques, sometimes little pruritus; highly infectious through skin scales

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcoptes scabiei females burrow into stratum corneum; delayed hypersensitivity to mite products produces symptoms
First infestation may remain asymptomatic for weeks; reinfestation causes faster symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: Typical distribution/contact history → clinical diagnosis; treatment need not await microscopic confirmation
★ **Mineral-oil skin scraping** of burrow → mites, eggs, or feces; negative scraping cannot exclude
Dermoscopy may reveal triangular mite at end of burrow

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Permethrin 5%** neck down, including folds/nails; wash after 8–14 hours; repeat in 1 week
Infants/young children: include scalp/neck; avoid eyes/mouth; sulfur alternative for infants <2 months
Oral ivermectin alternative: two treatments 7–14 days apart; avoid during pregnancy or weight <15 kg
★ Crusted disease → **oral ivermectin + repeated topical permethrin**, keratolytics and contact isolation
Residual itch may last weeks → topical corticosteroid/antihistamine; new burrows prompt reassessment for reinfestation

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary impetigo/cellulitis from scratching; poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis after infected lesions
Institutional outbreaks; persistent genital nodules may reflect hypersensitivity rather than living mites

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat household and sexual contacts simultaneously**, even without symptoms
Hot wash/dry recently used clothing and bedding; bag unwashable items for at least 72 hours
Avoid close skin contact until treatment completed; no insecticide fumigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atopic dermatitis: chronic flexural eczema, no burrows or household cluster
Bedbugs: exposed-skin grouped bites, environmental insects; no burrowing
Contact dermatitis: exposure-shaped eruption; contacts usually unaffected

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

stridor.name: Stridor
stridor.scope: Laryngomalacia (inspiratory, worse supine), tracheomalacia (expiratory), vocal cord dysfunction (paradoxical adduction), vascular ring (biphasic, dysphagia), flexible laryngoscopy
stridor.core: Harsh upper-airway noise: respiratory phase localizes obstruction; age, feeding difficulty, and episodic triggers identify the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Congenital airway abnormalities in infancy; prematurity, prior intubation, tracheoesophageal fistula → tracheal weakness
Exercise, stress, irritants → inducible laryngeal obstruction; aortic arch anomalies → extrinsic compression

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Retractions, cyanosis, apnea, exhaustion, or poor air movement** → impending respiratory failure
Feeding-associated choking, recurrent pneumonia, or poor growth → clinically significant obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inspiratory: extrathoracic collapse; expiratory: intrathoracic collapse; biphasic: fixed central obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable unexplained upper-airway noise → **awake flexible laryngoscopy**
Dynamic bronchoscopy assesses distal collapse; CT angiography/MR angiography delineates vascular compression
Normal examination between episodes does not exclude inducible obstruction; visualize during symptoms/exercise
Flow-volume loop: flattened inspiratory limb supports variable extrathoracic obstruction; not definitive alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Distress → oxygen, minimize agitation, **urgent controlled airway** with anesthesia/ENT
Mild congenital malacia → observation, feeding assessment, upright feeding while awake; spontaneous improvement with growth
★ Severe laryngeal collapse with apnea/poor growth → **supraglottoplasty**
Severe tracheal collapse → CPAP; refractory disease → airway surgery
Inducible obstruction → speech-guided breathing; symptomatic vascular ring → surgical division

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxemia, aspiration, recurrent respiratory infections, growth failure; severe obstruction → arrest
Misdiagnosed inducible obstruction → unnecessary bronchodilators, glucocorticoids, or intubations

rows.label: Prevention
items: Supine sleep on flat surface despite positional noise; no prone sleeping or wedges
Avoid smoke exposure; swallowing assessment and feeding modifications reduce aspiration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Croup: acute barky cough after URI; responds to dexamethasone
Foreign body: abrupt choking; rigid bronchoscopy despite normal radiograph
Epiglottitis: fever, drooling, tripod posture; avoid upsetting child or bedside throat examination

table.title: Chronic or episodic causes
rows: Expiratory; barking cough, worsens with exertion
Biphasic wheeze, dysphagia; steroid-unresponsive; neck extension relieves

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

syphilis.name: Syphilis
syphilis.scope: Primary syphilis, secondary syphilis, latent syphilis, tertiary syphilis, neurosyphilis, serologic testing, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, penicillin therapy
syphilis.core: Treponema pallidum infection progresses through mucocutaneous, asymptomatic, and destructive stages; neurologic, ocular, or auditory disease can occur anytime.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unprotected sex, multiple partners, HIV; transplacental transmission during pregnancy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Primary: **painless chancre** with regional lymphadenopathy
Secondary: palms/soles rash, condylomata lata, generalized nodes, patchy alopecia
Tertiary: gummas, ascending aortic aneurysm; tabes dorsalis, **Argyll Robertson pupils**, Charcot joint, or dementia
Latent: reactive serology without symptoms; early = acquired within 1 year

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Spirochete dissemination → endarteritis, young-adult meningovascular stroke; posterior column injury → sensory ataxia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RPR/VDRL + treponemal assay**; discordant reverse screen → second treponemal assay
Early chancre with negative serology → lesion testing or repeat serology
★ Neurologic deficits → **LP**; CSF-VDRL specific, negative result does not exclude
Quantitative RPR: early disease follow-up at 6/12 months; latent at 6/12/24 months
Tertiary disease → CSF assessment before treatment; isolated ocular/otic disease may not require LP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pregnancy with penicillin allergy → **desensitization**, then stage-specific penicillin
Nonpregnant penicillin allergy, uncomplicated early infection → doxycycline for 14 days

rows.label: Complications
items: Jarisch-Herxheimer: fever/myalgias within 24 hours after treatment; supportive care, not allergy
Congenital infection → stillbirth, hearing loss, dental/bone abnormalities

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Partners exposed within **90 days** → presumptive early-syphilis treatment despite negative tests
Condoms; HIV testing; prenatal screening; serial RPR after treatment, fourfold rise suggests reinfection/failure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chancroid: painful ulcer, tender suppurative nodes
HSV: painful grouped vesicles; pityriasis rosea: herald patch, usually spares palms
Autoimmune false-positive RPR: negative confirmatory treponemal assay

syphilis.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [CDC STI guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/syphilis.htm), including linked stage-specific guidance.

systemic-sclerosis.name: Systemic sclerosis
systemic-sclerosis.scope: Limited cutaneous (CREST syndrome, anti-centromere), diffuse cutaneous (anti-Scl-70, anti-RNA polymerase III), scleroderma renal crisis, pulmonary hypertension, interstitial lung disease, Raynaud
systemic-sclerosis.core: Autoimmune vasculopathy with skin tightening and organ fibrosis; cutaneous extent and antibody profile predict the major threats.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Female sex, middle adulthood, autoimmune predisposition; silica exposure
Early rapidly progressive diffuse skin disease and glucocorticoids increase renal-crisis risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Digital pits/ulcers, reduced oral aperture, abnormal nailfold capillaries; fixed contractures with advanced skin disease
Reflux/dysphagia from esophageal dysmotility; dry cough or exertional dyspnea signals lung involvement
★ **Abrupt hypertension + AKI**, sometimes MAHA → scleroderma renal crisis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury, obliterative vasculopathy, immune activation, and fibroblast collagen deposition
Renal arteriolar narrowing → renin-driven hypertension; collagen deposition → restrictive lung and gastrointestinal disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical phenotype plus **ANA and specific antibodies**; skin biopsy usually unnecessary
Baseline PFTs/DLCO and HRCT for ILD; echocardiography screens PAH, right-heart catheterization confirms
BP, creatinine, urinalysis; serial assessment detects renal injury before irreversible decline

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Renal crisis → immediate **captopril**, even with elevated creatinine; dialysis if needed
Raynaud → nifedipine; refractory digital ischemia → sildenafil or IV prostacyclin
Symptomatic reflux → omeprazole; ILD → mycophenolate, consider nintedanib for progressive fibrosis
PAH → specialist endothelin antagonist + PDE5 inhibitor; severe disease → prostacyclin
★ Avoid high-dose **glucocorticoids** when possible; no routine preventive ACE inhibitor solely for systemic sclerosis

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension/right-heart failure, interstitial fibrosis, digital gangrene
Esophageal stricture, small-bowel bacterial overgrowth, malnutrition; myocardial fibrosis/arrhythmias

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cold avoidance, smoking cessation, hand protection; exercise and range-of-motion work
Annual PAH assessment with echocardiography/DLCO; home BP checks, especially early diffuse disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary Raynaud: no tissue injury, normal nailfold capillaries, no systemic manifestations
Eosinophilic fasciitis: limb induration with eosinophilia, usually spares fingers and lacks Raynaud
Mixed connective tissue disease: anti-U1 RNP with overlapping myositis/arthritis features

table.title: Phenotype and antibodies
rows: CREST: calcinosis, Raynaud, esophageal dysfunction, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia
Rapid skin progression; anti-RNA polymerase III

systemic-vasculitis.name: Systemic vasculitis
systemic-vasculitis.scope: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA/PR3), microscopic polyangiitis (p-ANCA/MPO), eosinophilic GPA, polyarteritis nodosa, giant cell arteritis, Takayasu arteritis, immunosuppressive therapy
systemic-vasculitis.core: Vessel inflammation presenting as unexplained multisystem ischemia: vessel size, organ pattern, antibodies and tissue distinguish the syndromes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune predisposition; hydralazine/propylthiouracil can induce ANCA disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Constitutional symptoms, palpable purpura, skin ulcers, mononeuritis multiplex
★ **Hemoptysis + falling hemoglobin + RBC casts** → pulmonary–renal emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ANCA disease → pauci-immune necrotizing injury; larger-vessel inflammation → stenosis, thrombosis, aneurysms
Granulomas: GPA/EGPA, GCA/Takayasu; PAN: necrotizing medium-artery inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis, creatinine, CBC/differential, ESR/CRP**, chest imaging, hepatitis serologies
PR3/MPO supports diagnosis; negative ANCA cannot exclude, isolated positive cannot confirm
★ **Biopsy involved tissue**, especially kidney with GN; do not delay emergency therapy
GCA → temporal artery biopsy/expert ultrasound; **steroids before confirmation**
Takayasu → CTA/MRA; PAN → biopsy or visceral angiography showing microaneurysms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Organ-threatening disease → **urgent immunosuppression**; stabilize bleeding, renal failure, ischemia
GPA/MPA maintenance → rituximab/azathioprine; methotrexate if renal function permits
Plasma exchange not routine in ANCA; consider severe renal disease/anti-GBM overlap
GCA steroid sparing → tocilizumab; elective vascular reconstruction after inflammation controlled
HCV cryoglobulinemia → **direct-acting antivirals**, not immunosuppression alone; older questions may expect interferon-alfa

rows.label: Complications
items: Blindness, renal failure, stroke, bowel infarction, aortic aneurysm
Cyclophosphamide → infertility/cystitis/malignancy; rituximab → HBV reactivation; steroids → infection/osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **TMP-SMX** with cyclophosphamide/rituximab induction; HBV/TB testing before biologics
Vaccination, bone protection, fertility counseling; follow clinical findings, not ANCA titers alone

rows.label: Mimics
items: Endocarditis: positive blood cultures/vegetations; ANCA sometimes positive
Anti-GBM: linear IgG on renal biopsy
Cholesterol emboli: vascular procedure, blue toes, eosinophilia, preserved pulses

table.title: Disease signatures
rows: PR3/c-ANCA; destructive sinonasal/ear disease, cavitary lungs, GN
Severe disease: same induction as GPA
Steroids; severe → cyclophosphamide; nonsevere relapsing → mepolizumab
Age >50; jaw claudication, visual symptoms, PMR
Young women; pulse/BP discrepancy, arm claudication

testicular-cancer.name: Testicular cancer
testicular-cancer.scope: Seminoma, nonseminomatous germ cell tumors, sex cord-stromal tumors (Leydig cell, Sertoli cell), tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH), scrotal ultrasound, radical inguinal orchiectomy
testicular-cancer.core: A solid intratesticular lesion requires urgent evaluation for malignancy; an inguinal approach preserves proper staging and lymphatic drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Cryptorchidism**, prior contralateral germ cell tumor, family history, testicular dysgenesis
Most germ cell tumors arise in young adults; older men also require consideration of lymphoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually painless firm enlargement or heaviness; pain does not exclude malignancy
Gynecomastia from hormone production; back pain may indicate retroperitoneal nodes
Cough/dyspnea, supraclavicular nodes suggest dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Most adult tumors germ cell-derived; mixed tumors managed as nonseminomatous
Lymphatic spread follows gonadal vessels to retroperitoneal para-aortic nodes rather than initial inguinal drainage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler** first distinguishes intratesticular from extratesticular lesions
★ **AFP, β-hCG, LDH before orchiectomy**; repeat afterward for staging and response
CT abdomen/pelvis + chest imaging for metastases; normal markers do not exclude cancer
Avoid transscrotal needle biopsy or scrotal orchiectomy; disrupted lymphatics complicate treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Radical inguinal orchiectomy** for suspicious solid mass; discuss sperm banking before gonadotoxic treatment
Stage I seminoma: surveillance preferred when reliable; carboplatin or radiation selected alternatives
Stage I nonseminoma: surveillance, cisplatin-based chemotherapy, or retroperitoneal node dissection according to risk
★ Metastatic germ cell tumor → cisplatin-based **BEP**; residual nonseminomatous mass may require resection
Sex cord-stromal tumors: surgery; monitor endocrine manifestations and malignant features

rows.label: Complications
items: Infertility, hypogonadism; assess contralateral function
BEP: bleomycin pulmonary toxicity; cisplatin nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity; etoposide-associated leukemia
Retroperitoneal node surgery may cause retrograde ejaculation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Orchiopexy reduces cryptorchid-associated risk but does not eliminate it; no routine population screening
Strict stage-specific surveillance with examination, markers, and imaging after treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hydrocele: transilluminates; ultrasound needed if testis not palpable
Epididymitis: tender epididymis, urinary/infectious symptoms
Torsion: abrupt severe pain, absent cremasteric reflex; immediate exploration when strongly suspected

toxic-alcohol-poisoning.name: Toxic alcohol poisoning
toxic-alcohol-poisoning.scope: Ethylene glycol (calcium oxalate, renal failure), methanol (visual impairment, optic disc hyperemia), isopropyl alcohol (ketosis without acidosis), osmolar gap, fomepizole, hemodialysis
toxic-alcohol-poisoning.core: Unexplained intoxication with an osmolar gap suggests toxic alcohol exposure; delayed organic-acid accumulation can produce profound anion-gap acidosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antifreeze, windshield-washer fluid, solvents; accidental ingestion or self-harm; substitute alcohol consumption

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting, abdominal pain, altered consciousness; tachypnea or shock signals severe toxicity
★ **Normal osmolar gap does not exclude late poisoning**; history may be unavailable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alcohol dehydrogenase converts parent alcohols into characteristic metabolites
Parent compounds elevate osmolar gap early; metabolites later raise anion gap in acid-producing ingestions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Electrolytes, ABG/VBG, glucose, BUN, measured osmolality, ethanol and specific alcohol levels
Calculated osmolality = 2Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8; add ethanol/4.6, concentrations in mg/dL
Measured minus calculated >10 mOsm/kg supports exposure; nonspecific and time-dependent
Urinalysis and calcium/creatinine assess organ injury; absent characteristic sediment inclusions do not exclude exposure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway, IV fluids, poison-center consultation; **fomepizole** immediately for suspected methanol/ethylene glycol
Methanol: vision loss, coma/seizures or pH ≤7.15 → **hemodialysis**; ethylene glycol: severe acidosis/AKI → dialysis
Sodium bicarbonate for marked acidemia; methanol → folinic acid; ethylene glycol → thiamine/pyridoxine adjuncts
★ Isopropanol → supportive care; **avoid fomepizole**, which prolongs parent-compound toxicity

rows.label: Complications
items: Methanol: permanent blindness, basal ganglia injury
Oxalate toxicity: hypocalcemic dysrhythmias; any ingestion: aspiration, coma, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: Store products separately from beverages; child-resistant containers; suicide-risk assessment after intentional ingestion

rows.label: Mimics
items: DKA: hyperglycemia and β-hydroxybutyrate elevation
Alcoholic ketoacidosis: poor intake after alcohol binge, low/normal glucose

toxic-alcohol-poisoning.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [EXTRIP methanol](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/methanol), [ethylene glycol](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/ethylene-glycol); other principles: established toxicology teaching.

tuberculosis.name: Tuberculosis
tuberculosis.scope: Latent TB infection screening (PPD, IGRA), treatment regimens, active pulmonary TB, acid-fast bacilli smear and culture, RIPE therapy, extrapulmonary TB (Pott disease)
tuberculosis.core: Chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, and upper-lobe cavitation suggest contagious pulmonary tuberculosis; latent infection has no active disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Close contact, endemic residence, incarceration, homelessness, crowding, **long-term care** work/volunteering
HIV, TNF inhibitors, transplant, silicosis, diabetes → progression/reactivation risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Hemoptysis, prolonged fever; primary disease may cause hilar adenopathy or pleural effusion
★ **Back pain with vertebral destruction** → Pott disease; miliary spread causes diffuse micronodules
Tuberculous pleurisy: **lymphocytic exudate**, high protein, low glucose

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Airborne bacilli survive in macrophages; T-cell granulomas contain infection; T-cell dysfunction → reactivation, skin-test anergy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screening: **IGRA** preferred after BCG; TST read induration at 48–72 hours
Positive screening → symptoms + chest radiograph; neither test distinguishes latent from active infection
★ Active suspicion → **sputum NAAT, AFB smear, culture and susceptibility**; collect serial specimens
Negative smear, TST or IGRA does not exclude active TB, especially with immunosuppression or malnutrition
Pott suspicion → spinal MRI, biopsy/culture; assess cord compression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected contagious disease → **airborne isolation** and public-health notification
Drug-susceptible active TB: 2 months isoniazid/rifampin/pyrazinamide/ethambutol → 4 months isoniazid/rifampin
Eligible pulmonary cases ≥12 years: 4-month isoniazid/rifapentine/moxifloxacin/pyrazinamide-based regimen alternative
Latent, no RIPE: 3-month isoniazid/rifapentine or 4-month rifampin; older questions may expect **isoniazid** alone, still acceptable
Isoniazid → pyridoxine prevents neuropathy, sideroblastic anemia; Pott with deficit/instability → urgent spinal surgery evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Meningitis, adrenal destruction, spinal cord compression, bronchiectasis
INH/rifampin/pyrazinamide: hepatotoxicity; ethambutol: optic neuropathy; rifampin: enzyme induction, orange secretions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Contact investigation**, latent-treatment completion; directly observed active treatment improves adherence
Review drug interactions and baseline liver risk; monitor visual acuity/color vision with ethambutol

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung cancer: focal malignant biopsy
Fungal infection: geographic exposure; nontuberculous mycobacteria: species identification distinguishes

table.title: Positive TST thresholds
rows: HIV, close contacts, transplant, substantial immunosuppression
Healthcare workers, exposure-risk groups, comorbidities, young children

tumor-lysis-syndrome.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
tumor-lysis-syndrome.scope: Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, acute kidney injury, allopurinol, rasburicase, aggressive hydration
tumor-lysis-syndrome.core: Rapid malignant-cell destruction causes an electrolyte and urate emergency; anticipate risk before cancer treatment and respond immediately to evolving organ dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Burkitt/high-grade lymphoma, acute leukemia, bulky chemosensitive tumors, high LDH or leukocyte count
Renal impairment, dehydration, high baseline urate; cytotoxics, steroids, targeted drugs; sometimes spontaneous

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, weakness, muscle cramps, paresthesias or tetany shortly after treatment
★ **Oliguria, arrhythmia, seizure** signal clinical disease; abnormalities may precede symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intracellular potassium/phosphate and nucleic acids released; purine breakdown produces uric acid
Urate and calcium-phosphate precipitation injure kidneys; phosphate binding reduces serum calcium

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Check **K, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine**, LDH; ECG and continuous telemetry
Laboratory TLS: ≥2 abnormalities within 24 hours, from 3 days pretreatment through 7 days posttreatment
Clinical TLS: laboratory pattern plus AKI, arrhythmia/sudden death, or seizure
High-risk/established disease → repeat electrolytes and renal indices every 4–6 hours; strict intake/output

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic saline**, individualized to cardiac/renal status; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids
★ Dangerous hyperkalemia → **IV calcium for ECG changes**, insulin/dextrose; dialysis for refractory abnormalities
Established hyperuricemia/high-risk TLS → rasburicase; screen **G6PD**, contraindicated if deficient
Phosphate restriction/binders; avoid treating asymptomatic hypocalcemia; symptomatic tetany/seizures → cautious calcium
Urgent dialysis: refractory K/phosphate, acidosis, symptomatic hypocalcemia, fluid overload, or worsening oliguric AKI

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute renal failure, life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia, seizures, sudden death
Rasburicase → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; allopurinol → hypersensitivity and xanthine crystal burden

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Risk-stratify before treatment; **allopurinol + hydration** for intermediate risk; rasburicase for high risk
Allopurinol prevents new urate formation; does not remove existing uric acid
Avoid urinary alkalinization → calcium-phosphate precipitation; no routine concurrent allopurinol and rasburicase

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rhabdomyolysis: markedly elevated CK and myoglobinuria, muscle injury context
Isolated AKI: electrolyte retention without abrupt tumor-destruction pattern
Sepsis: infection-associated organ dysfunction; can coexist and trigger tumor lysis

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired glucose uptake + excess hepatic output; early compensatory **↑serum insulin**, later relative secretory failure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin; **lactic acidosis**: avoid eGFR <30, AKI/sepsis, hypoxia; no new start <45; reduce 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**
Otherwise GLP-1 RA before insulin; older exam questions may expect **basal insulin** once two orals fail
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain
Metformin: GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; pioglitazone: edema, HF; sulfonylureas: labeled caution with sulfa allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot and dilated eye examinations** (eye spacing by findings)
★ Albuminuria + hypertension → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**, never both; efferent dilation ↓intraglomerular pressure
BP ≥130/80 → antihypertensive; older exam questions may expect ACE inhibitor, also normotensive albuminuria
Statin age 40–75; glycemic control slows **neuropathy**, retinopathy, nephropathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, inherited thrombophilia
**Previous VTE** is the strongest predictor of recurrence; remote surgery months ago adds little
**Central venous catheter** → main cause of upper-extremity DVT

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload
Massive PE: high RA/PA pressure, low PCWP, low output; RV infarct: PA pressure normal/low

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week
Low-probability V/Q + high clinical suspicion is nondiagnostic → **CT angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; cancer → LMWH/DOAC; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible
Acute proximal DVT/PE without DOAC → immediate **heparin**; warfarin alone never initial; inferior in cancer

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Aspirin or 1 month inadequate; DOACs now preferred, older exam questions may expect warfarin 3–6 months
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization
Hip arthroplasty → LMWH, warfarin or DOAC; aspirin now accepted, older exam questions may expect anticoagulant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
Amniotic fluid embolism: peripartum collapse with **DIC/low fibrinogen**

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

vertigo.name: Vertigo
vertigo.scope: Peripheral vs central vertigo, benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (Dix-Hallpike, Epley maneuver), vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis, Meniere disease, vestibular migraine
vertigo.core: Illusion of movement: timing, triggers, hearing findings and neurologic examination distinguish benign vestibular disease from posterior-circulation ischemia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, vascular risk factors → central ischemia; recent viral illness, head injury or migraine history
Ototoxic drugs and ear disease can cause peripheral vestibular injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Peripheral: horizontal-torsional unidirectional nystagmus, reduced with fixation; no focal neurologic deficit
★ **Vertical/direction-changing nystagmus, skew deviation, severe truncal ataxia or focal deficits** → central concern
New unilateral hearing loss with continuous acute vertigo can represent AICA stroke, not simply labyrinthitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Asymmetric vestibular input → movement illusion and nystagmus; central lesions involve brainstem/cerebellum
BPPV: displaced **otoliths (canaliths)** in semicircular canal → position-triggered endolymph movement

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Dix-Hallpike** for triggered episodic symptoms; typical upbeat torsional nystagmus has latency and fatigues
Continuous acute syndrome with spontaneous nystagmus → **HINTS by trained clinician**; not for brief positional episodes
★ Normal head impulse, direction-changing nystagmus or skew → **stroke evaluation/MRI ± CTA/MRA**
Untrained examiner or concerning findings → MRI; early diffusion imaging may miss posterior stroke
Typical BPPV → no routine imaging; suspected Meniere → audiometry; horizontal positional nystagmus → supine-roll test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Central concern → urgent **stroke pathway**; negative head CT cannot exclude posterior infarction
Severe acute nausea → brief meclizine/ondansetron; prolonged vestibular suppressants impair compensation

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, dehydration, impaired driving; missed stroke → disability/death; recurrent inner-ear disease → hearing loss

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fall precautions, avoid driving during attacks; reduce individual migraine triggers and address vascular risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Orthostatic hypotension: standing-triggered presyncope with BP drop, rather than head-position-triggered nystagmus
Arrhythmia: episodic faintness/palpitations; ECG or monitoring establishes cardiac cause

table.title: Peripheral and episodic patterns
rows: Rehabilitation; discuss early steroids, benefit uncertain
